name: Andres Quintero
title: Board Vice President, Alum Rock Union Elementary School District
years_of_service: 2022 to 2026 (current term, per the district's board directory; not stated whether this is his first term or a re-election).
background: Quintero is the sitting Board Vice President of the Alum Rock Union Elementary School District Board of Trustees. He held that role at the district's July 16, 2026 meeting, when the board adopted Resolution No. 01-26/27 placing Measure O (a renewed $310 parcel tax) and Resolution No. 02-26/27 placing Measure P (a $100 million general obligation bond) on the November 3, 2026 ballot; full detail on both measures is covered in content/measures/scc-measure-o-2026.json and content/measures/scc-measure-p-2026.json and not duplicated here. The district's board directory lists his current term as 2022 to 2026 but gives no prior term history, election date, or vote margin.

I was not able to independently verify Quintero's occupation, education, prior public offices, committee assignments outside the board, or specific named votes beyond the two 2026 ballot resolutions. This session's WebSearch tool had exhausted its query budget before his profile was researched (a direct search for his name returned a budget-exhausted message), and direct WebFetch attempts at the ARUSD board of trustees page and the district's general About Us page returned only his name, title, contact information, and term dates, with no biography, news release, or press coverage found. A Ballotpedia lookup for 'Andres Quintero' returned no page matching this district. Because of that, committee_memberships, voting_record_highlights, and endorsements_received are left empty below rather than populated with unverified claims.
attendance: No individually published meeting-attendance or voting-participation record for Trustee Quintero was found. Alum Rock Union Elementary School District does not appear to publish a per-trustee attendance scorecard on its public board pages; board agendas and minutes are available via the district's board-materials system (see the July 16, 2026 board book cited in the Measure O and Measure P sources), which would in principle allow a manual tally of attendance and votes, but compiling that was not feasible within this session's tool budget (WebSearch exhausted, and several direct district-site fetches returned no usable content).
